# Generator-shortcuts answer

The strongest plausible shortcut that fits every canonical demonstration is **main-diagonal-only filling**: for a repeated color, fill its bounding rectangle only when the second corner is down-and-right from the first; leave an anti-diagonal pair unchanged. All five canonical inputs happen to use only the top-left-to-bottom-right orientation, so this rival reproduces all five canonical outputs exactly.

The exact lawful counterexample is stored in `repo/generators/1d23d72f3b43/counterexamples/main_diagonal_only.json`. It is an 8×8 grid containing color 4 at `(0,0)` and `(2,2)`, plus color 7 at `(4,6)` and `(6,4)`. The intended rule fills both 3×3 boxes. The rival fills the color-4 box but leaves only the two color-7 corner cells, disagreeing on seven cells.

I checked the intended output through the selected canonical Racket rule with:

`python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 1d23d72f3b43 --input ../checks/counterexample-orientation/input.json --out ../checks/counterexample-orientation/racket.json`

The receipt records rule hash `013675ae7255`, final generator SHA-256 `36a6069b7fa9fc4438410b6321dbe760ef493008780c86328ad4fca686d2461b`, and a valid output. A focused regression test independently reconstructs the intended output, executes the declared rival, and verifies the disagreement.

Yes, the repaired generator emits such cases. Every ordinary draw has at least one anti-diagonal pair and one main-diagonal pair. The strict semantic census observed the anti-diagonal witness in 600/600 final-source draws, and the 300-lesson source-bound census found 0 ambiguities in 1,200 production pairs and 0 ambiguities in 1,200 query rotations against the declared rival.
